# cancho-quantum

> A small state-vector quantum simulator written in cancho, built to test what a linear-types-and-capabilities language catches in quantum code. Pre-PoC; milestones M0 to M3 are done, plus more gates, sampling, OpenQASM input and algorithms (see docs/features-results.md). Everything here is measured against cancho compiler revision 3fa3fbb.

## Read first
- [README](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-quantum/blob/main/README.md): the commands.
- [Design and must-reject list](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-quantum/blob/main/docs/qubit-types.md): what the checker should refuse, and what it cannot.
- [M2 results](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-quantum/blob/main/docs/m2-results.md): the five must-reject entries; four are refused, one is not.
- [Features: gates, sampling, OpenQASM, algorithms](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-quantum/blob/main/docs/features-results.md)
- [Agent prompt](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-quantum/blob/main/docs/agent-prompt.md): install and try it, no key, no model.

## Facts an agent should not get wrong
- A `Qubit` is a `res`: it cannot be copied or dropped; `qubit.measure` is the only function that ends one.
- Refusals carry a stable rule tag: read `cancho check ... --output json`, field `rule`. Do not match on the message.
- CNOT with one qubit as both operands is accepted by the checker and stops at run time (a trap). Do not report it as a refusal.
- `Qubit { ... }` can be written directly from any module; `qubit.fresh` is a convention.
- The aarch64 determinism result is emulation under qemu-user, not arm64 hardware.
- Circuit text format: `n N`, then `h|x|y|z|s|sdg|t|tdg q`, `cx|cz|swap a b`, `ccx c1 c2 t`, `rx|ry|rz|p q num den` and `cp a b num den` (theta = pi*num/den), `seed S`, `m q`, `sample N` (up to 4096, no collapse), `bitflip|phaseflip|depol|ampdamp q num den`, `depol2 a b num den`, `readout num den` (each measured/sampled bit is reported flipped; the state is not changed), `model1|model2 num den` (depolarizing noise after every one- or two-qubit gate; num 0 turns it off), `gate1err q num den`, `gate2err a b num den`, `coher q T1 T2` (nanoseconds, T2 <= 2 T1), `wait q ns`, `time1 ns`, `time2 ns`, `dur1 q ns`, `dur2 a b ns` (idle decay: amplitude damping then dephasing, also after each gate for its duration; `sched` starts every gate as soon as its qubits are free so a qubit waiting for a partner decays too, `barrier` waits for all; `docs/idle-noise.md`), `readerr q n01 d01 n10 d10` (per-qubit/per-pair overrides and asymmetric readout; `tools/qprofile.cho` (cancho) writes them from a JSON device profile on standard input, and `profiles/example_5q.json` is INVENTED, not a real machine; `profiles/ibm_perth_2024-05-27.json` is IBM's published calibration of a real 7-qubit device, converted by `tools/qcalib.cho` (cancho) from `profiles/raw/ibm_perth_props_2024-05-27.json`, see `docs/calibration.md`) (noise with probability num/den; in `n` mode by trajectories, so one run is one noisy outcome and only the average is the physics; in `dm` mode exact), `trig num den`. A header `dm N` in place of `n N` runs the density matrix instead (exact noise, N up to 10; extra ops `purity`, `trace`, `probs`; no `sample`, no QASM, interpreted only). A file starting `OPENQASM` is read as OpenQASM 2.0 (an angle is a decimal in radians, `pi`, or a multiple of pi such as `3*pi/4`; a decimal is read to the double Python reads, checked on 18,252 texts); also cy ch crz rzz cswap, up to four cregs, `measure q[i] -> c[j]` and `if (c==k) stmt`; no `gate` definitions yet.
- Noise in `n` mode is sampled: do not read one run as the mixed state. Use `dm` for the exact state.
- Repeating a qubit in a multi-qubit gate (cx q q, swap q q, ccx with a repeat) type-checks and traps at run time. Qiskit refuses it when the circuit is built; here it is a trap, not a refusal.

## Checks
- `python3 scripts/check_types.py`: 24 accept/reject fixtures.
- `python3 scripts/check_noise.py`: noisy runs averaged over many seeds against an exact density-matrix calculation (needs qiskit).
- `python3 scripts/check_profile.py`: the noise-profile converter and its use, against Qiskit.
- `python3 scripts/check_qasm.py`: OpenQASM files agree between Qiskit's parser and qsim, and random circuits of sx sxdg id u2 u3 u cx h written by Qiskit give its statevector (needs qiskit).
- `python3 scripts/check_diff.py`: amplitudes against Qiskit (needs qiskit, numpy).
- `python3 scripts/check_determinism.py [--arm64]`: byte-identical output across builds.
- `QSIM=... ML=... python3 scripts/rates_sim.py`: gate error rates recovered by `ml fit --model linear` from simulated mirror circuits, against known answers (cancho-ml; docs/rates-regression.md).
- `STATS=... python3 scripts/hw_gof.py JOB.json`: chi-square test (cancho-stats) of a hardware run against the model (docs/hardware.md, last section).
- `CANCHO=... QSIM=... STATS=... ML=... OPT=... python3 scripts/check_hw.py`: `tools/hw/` (the hardware analysis as one cancho program: `hw model|gof|mitigate|predict|rates|fit JOB`; it spawns `qsim`, `qmitigate`, cancho-stats `stats`, cancho-ml `ml` and cancho-opt `opt`) against the Python scripts `hw_model/hw_gof/hw_mitigate/hw_predict/hw_rates.py`, on the committed runs, to 1e-9; `hw fit` against the committed `fit-global-*.json` of `hw_fit.py` (100 s, same 118 evaluations). Authority: files, exec and clock, not narrowed.
- `CANCHO=... OPT=... python3 scripts/check_vqe.py`: `examples/vqe` (a VQE of a 4-qubit Ising chain on cancho-opt's `opt minimize`, BFGS with parameter-shift gradients, Nelder-Mead, or SPSA for the sampled energy) against numpy and scipy, eighteen mutants killed; shot noise, read-out error and mitigation checked statistically (examples/vqe/README.md).
- `python3 scripts/check_scan.py`: `tools/qscan.cho` (a read-out scan of a device as `qsim` `readerr` operations) against its Python reference and in `qsim`.
- `python3 scripts/check_mitigate.py`: `tools/qmitigate.cho` (read-out error mitigation of measured counts) against its Python reference and the physics.
- `python3 scripts/check_hw_spike.py`: the pre-flight read-out check of `scripts/hw_spike.py` finds broken qubits (offline).
- `python3 scripts/hw_summary.py --check`: the hardware numbers on the landing page match docs/data/hardware/.
- `sh scripts/site.sh --check`: the landing page matches the tools (built by cancho, `tools/site/`); `python3 scripts/check_site.py` compares it with the Python reference builder.
